articles.title: El retorno de Aleksandre Topuria, más cerca que nunca
articles.standfirst: 'El Conquistador' apunta a volver a pelear en UFC antes de que acabe al año
articles.summary: 'El Conquistador' apunta a volver a pelear en UFC antes de que acabe al año
articles.body: Dos peleas en UFC y dos victorias para Aleksandre Topuria (7-1)... pero la carrera de 'El Conquistador' está en 'stand-by' desde el pasado 22 de noviembre. Puede ser esa la fecha de su regreso al octágono, pero en este 2026... y de nuevo en Qatar. La información ha salido a escena: el equipo de Santiago Luna (8-1) ha filtrado que la UFC les ha ofrecido la pelea y que se está negociando. MARCA, sin embargo, puede confirmar que el 'staff' de Aleksandre no ha recibido todavía ningún ofrecimiento. Lo que no quita que este combate pueda hacerse para el próximo 21 de noviembre, fecha deslizada por 'MMA Latinoamérica' en redes sociales. Si la oferta llega, aceptarán. Desde el entorno de Aleksandre Topuria lo tienen claro. En caso de ser real el rumor, todo debería precipitarse esta semana o principios de la próxima. Y eso que no es un combate que favorezca demasiado a los intereses del hispanogeorgiano: Luna no está rankeado y viene de perder ante Bryce Mitchell. Es decir, no haría subir demasiado al mayor de los Topuria en caso de victoria. Tiene más que perder... que ganar. Sin embargo, Aleksandre solamente suma dos combates en UFC (dos victorias) en casi dos años desde su debut... y necesita actividad. Mientras Ilia se recupera de sus lesiones (no volverá hasta pasado el mes de febrero de 2027), el mayor de los Topuria debe dar un paso al frente.

images.caption: Aleksandre Topuria, durante un pesaje ceremonial de la UFC. UFC.

articles.title: Jon Jones Train Partner Hints at Possible UFC Return Following Tom Aspinall Injury News
articles.summary: Jon Jones appears to be reconsidering his future in mixed martial arts now that the UFC heavyweight picture has been […]
articles.body:
Jon Jones appears to be reconsidering his future in mixed martial arts now that the UFC heavyweight picture has been thrown into chaos once again.

Earlier this week, Tom Aspinall announced he had vacated the heavyweight title due to his ongoing injuries. The plan had been for Aspinall to rematch Ciryl Gane at UFC 334, but after re-injuring himself in training, the 33-year-old decided he did not want to hold up the division while his return timeline remained unknown.

Aspinall dropping the title drew a reaction from Jones, who questioned the legitimacy of the injury. The two never actually fought, despite Aspinall serving as interim heavyweight champion during Jones' reign atop the division. Jones avoided the matchup at every opportunity and reportedly turned down a $30 million offer from the UFC to make it happen, a stretch that ultimately led to his first retirement from the sport in June 2025 and Aspinall's promotion to undisputed champion.

Jones briefly walked that retirement back and re-entered the UFC's testing pool, but officially retired for good this past April. According to training partner Gable Steveson, Aspinall's title vacation has reignited his interest in competing again.

"I think Ciryl Gane deserves (the undisputed title) he's a fantastic fighter and he's a guy that goes out there and he's beating everybody besides the infinity stones of fighting, (Francis) Ngannou and Jon," Steveson told RMC Sport Combat when asked about the state of the heavyweight division.

"I think Jon would like to come back also, maybe seeing this belt open up put another fire into him. Jon's my training partner everyday in Albuquerque so I've seen what he can still do and I know he can do it at the highest level, and maybe his time will come again and I think it will," Steveson added.

Despite Steveson's comments suggesting Jones is eyeing a comeback, it remains unclear whether UFC CEO Dana White would entertain that possibility at this stage.

With Aspinall stepping away from the title, Gane will be elevated to undisputed champion, since he already holds the interim belt. Gane has received multiple callouts for his first defense, with Josh Hokit requesting a title shot and recent rival Alex Pereira doing the same.

There is speculation that Pereira is the frontrunner to land the fight with Gane, continuing a rematch campaign he has pushed for over the past several months.

Opinion: Jones Returning Would Be A Mistake Worth Making Anyway

Jones sitting out the Aspinall era was always going to invite second-guessing, and Aspinall vacating the belt gives him the cleanest opening yet to walk back his retirement without directly confronting the man he spent years avoiding. That distinction matters more than it might seem. Jones can frame a return as chasing an open title rather than finally answering Aspinall's callouts, which is exactly the kind of narrative control he has built his late career around.

Whether White actually wants this is a separate question, and a fair one. Jones' history of pulling out of fights, combined with a heavyweight division that finally has real momentum behind Gane and Pereira, makes it reasonable for the promotion to move on without him. But UFC has rarely turned down a Jones headline when one was available, and a heavyweight picture this unsettled is exactly the kind of moment that tends to pull him back in.

If Jones does return, expect the promotion to build it around the vacant title rather than a direct Aspinall fight, at least initially. That keeps the door open for the matchup everyone still wants to see, without forcing either side into a fight neither seemed eager to have when it actually mattered.

articles.title: Gable Steveson reacts to Tom Aspinall relinquishing UFC title
articles.summary: Gable Steveson sees Tom Aspinall's title resignation as an opportunity.
articles.body:
In light of Tom Aspinall vacating his UFC title, Gable Steveson has a mixed reaction to the news.

After almost a year away from the octagon, Aspinall has finally relinquished his UFC gold. The Brit is still suffering from the aftermath of an illegal eye poke that ended his UFC 321 title defense prematurely; undergoing several successful surgeries. Now with no undisputed champion in place, the division can move forward. Vocal in their pursuit of a title opportunity, some heavyweights have spoken out on social media about the possibility of fighting for the abandoned throne.

Josh Hokit has been the loudest , claiming that he deserves a shot and has called out interim champion Ciryl Gane to accompany him in the cage. While many believe Hokit deserves his shot, one man who is confident he'll find himself in the title picture soon is Gable Steveson .

But instead of kicking Tom Aspinall while he's down, Steveson offered some words of encouragement for the former titleholder.

"I feel for Tom," Steveson said. "I hope the recovery is going well, and as he posted, it seems like it's really not. So, prayers to him and his family, and make sure he can get back on his feet in the best way possible."

Steveson also knows Tom Aspinall's absence leaves a gaping hole in the weight class. The Olympian is ready to capitalize on the void, believing he is one step closer to UFC gold due to Aspinall's injury.

"I think this is a great opportunity for a lot of young guys like myself, and a few others that are in the heavyweight division to kind of sneak our way in and work hard and get to where we need to go, and in a faster transition," Steveson added.

"So, sorry to him for these complications, but I feel like it's a good thing for us."

images.caption: Gable Steveson reacts to Tom Aspinall relinquishing UFC title

articles.title: Ilia Topuria vuelve con todo: "La próxima vez me aseguraré de que revisen los guantes de Justin para que no les ponga nada raro"
articles.standfirst: El 'Matador' lanzó un mensaje en su cuenta de Twitter
articles.summary: El 'Matador' lanzó un mensaje en su cuenta de Twitter
articles.body: Y en su primer tuit tres meses después, Ilia Topuria (17-1) volvió con todo. El 'Matador', que está en Miami completando su recuperación y empezando poco a poco su vuelta a los entrenamientos, lanzó un mensaje en sus redes sociales avisando de su retorno... y con un dardo a Justin Gaethje (28-5), el nuevo campeón del peso ligero tras coronarse en UFC Casa Blanca. Este fue el mensaje de Ilia Topuria: "Últimas pruebas médicas hechas. He vuelto. A todos los payasos que han estado hablando mal de mí y dándome por perdido todo este tiempo, aquí estoy. Ahora veamos quién tiene pelotas. Gracias a todos por el apoyo. La próxima vez me aseguraré de que revisen los guantes de Justin para que no les ponga nada raro. Nos vemos pronto". El peleador ahora afincado en Miami entró de lleno en la polémica que hubo post-combate sobre los guantes de Gaethje. Muchos aficionados insinuaron (sin pruebas) que el estadounidense había alterado sus guantes introduciendo algo en su anterior para que los golpes impactaran con mayor fuerza en el cuerpo y rostro del 'Matador'. Un asunto que se había disipado con el paso de los meses... pero que ahora está de vuelta por el tuit de Topuria. Durante toda su carrera, el doble campeón hispanogeorgiano había habituado a sus fans a ser un usuario activo en Twitter. Y ahora, ya recuperado de sus lesiones en UFC Casa Blanca, Topuria está de vuelta en todos los aspectos. Ilia caldea el ambiente de cara a una posible revancha con Gaethje, que es lo que tanto él como su equipo buscan: recuperar el título del peso ligero lo más pronto posible y demostrar que el pasado 14 de junio únicamente fue una mala noche.

images.caption: Ilia Topuria, tras ganar a Charles Oliveira. UFC.

articles.title: Ilia Topuria ‘back’ after clearing medical tests, blames Justin Gaethje’s ‘weird’ gloves for UFC White House loss
articles.summary: Ilia Topuria is officially back — and apparently armed with one of the wildest excuses imaginable. The former two-division Ultimate Fighting Championship (UF...
articles.body:
Ilia Topuria is officially back — and apparently armed with one of the wildest excuses imaginable.

The former two-division Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) champion announced today (Weds., Sept. 16, 2026) that he has completed his final medical tests and is cleared to resume his career following the horrific beating he suffered against Justin Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 in June 2026.

However, buried inside Topuria's fiery return announcement was an absolutely insane suggestion that Gaethje may have loaded or otherwise tampered with his gloves before handing "El Matador" the first loss of his professional career.

"Final medical tests done. I'm back," Topuria wrote on Twitter. "To all the clowns who've been talking shit and counting me out this whole time, here I am. Now let's see who's got the balls. Thanks to everyone for the support. Next time I'll make sure they check Justin's gloves so he doesn't put anything weird on them. See you soon."

"By the way Justin, f—k you. And Ali, f—k you too."

Yes, Topuria genuinely appears to be buying into the ridiculous conspiracy theory pushed by a small portion of his fanbase following UFC White House.

The theory claimed Gaethje had something illegal inside his gloves — or "bricks," as "The Highlight" jokingly described it — because of the extraordinary damage he inflicted upon Topuria. Gaethje and longtime head coach Trevor Wittman already laughed off the baseless accusations during an appearance on The Joe Rogan Experience .

"What a compliment," Gaethje said. "People saying I'm juiced, what a compliment. People saying I've got bricks in my f—king gloves, what a compliment."

There has been zero credible evidence that Gaethje tampered with his gloves, loaded his hand wraps or did anything illegal before the fight. No commission official or UFC representative has raised concerns about Gaethje's equipment.

Gaethje simply beat the hell out of Topuria.

After surviving a dangerous second round, Gaethje took control and battered the previously undefeated champion until Topuria's corner stopped the fight before the fifth round. Topuria suffered two broken orbital bones and severe facial damage and was immediately transported to a local hospital .

The glove accusation is also a dramatic departure from Topuria's original reaction. In his first statement after the loss, Topuria insisted there were "no excuses," acknowledged Gaethje's performance , and admitted his rival had delivered on his promise to leave a mark on his face.

Three months later, the excuses have arrived.

Topuria did not reveal when he plans to compete again or whether UFC will grant him an immediate rematch. UFC CEO Dana White recently confirmed that Topuria is ready to return and expressed interest in either a second Gaethje fight or the long-awaited grudge match against Paddy Pimblett .

Whenever Topuria returns, he may want to focus on correcting the tactical mistakes that cost him the title instead of checking Gaethje's gloves for imaginary foreign objects.

images.caption: WASHINGTON, DC - JUNE 13: UFC lightweight fighter Ilia Topuria poses during the ceremonial weigh-in during the UFC Freedom 250 Fan Fest on The Ellipse ahead of the upcoming UFC Freedom 250 fight on the South Lawn of the White House on June 13, 2026 in Washington, DC. President Trump is hosting a series of Ultimate Fighting Championship matches on his 80th birthday on June 14, which the White House is calling "a once-in-a-generation celebration of the American fighting spirit." (Photo by Al Drago/Getty Images) | Getty Images

articles.title: Chael Sonnen apologizes to Tom Aspinall over injury drama: 'We got this wrong'
articles.summary: "I feel terrible for the guy," the UFC Hall of Famer said of Aspinall. "If there's any injury I could have, the last one I would want is something with my ey...
articles.body:
It already seemed as if it couldn't get any worse for Tom Aspinall and his pursuit of an active UFC heavyweight championship reign. Then, complications from his lingering eye injuries led him to vacate the title .

Aspinall announced Monday on social media that he was giving up the title he originally won as an interim championship in November 2023. That same title later became undisputed when Jon Jones retired and relinquished his belt in June 2025. In Aspinall's first defense of the undisputed title in October 2025, he infamously fought to a first-round no-contest against Ciryl Gane after suffering multiple grisly eye-pokes .

Given how common eye-pokes have been throughout UFC history, the length of Aspinall's injury woes sparked widespread speculation on their legitimacy. Even pundits and UFC Hall of Famers like Chael Sonnen questioned what was going on with Aspinall.

After the saga reached the point of Aspinall giving up the title, Sonnen apologized to the now-former champion on Tuesday's edition of "The Ariel Helwani Show."

"I'm so sorry for what Tom Aspinall went through, and I even look back at some of my words and opinions that were clearly wrong. There is clearly a medical issue here," Sonnen told Uncrowned.

"We got this wrong. Guys get poked in the eye all the time, and they keep on fighting. Then, when the stakes were this big, we didn't know. We got it wrong, and I feel terrible for the guy. If there's any injury I could have, the last one I would want is something with my eyes.

"That's a very real life thing that can impact you. You've got to be very careful."

In Aspinall's absence, the man who infamously fouled him, Gane, claimed a newly-created interim title by defeating Alex Pereira at UFC Freedom 250 on the White House's South Lawn in June. The UFC has yet to make a public statement on whether or not Aspinall's decision automatically makes Gane the new undisputed heavyweight champion.

Regardless of how the divisional landscape shakes out, Sonnen expects Aspinall won't lose his seat atop the division once he's ready to return. Sonnen compared the situation to those of past champions like Georges St-Pierre, who gave up their titles mid-reign or at the peak of their powers.

"Tom's going to be back, and when he is, he's going to be in that exact same spot, right?" Sonnen said. "He's going to be fighting in a main event for the undisputed heavyweight championship of the world. Things in his life are not going to change, so this is just purely a 'get-well, Tom.'

"I do think it was handled right. I do think that it was handled with grace, and I think that aside from the UFC doing it right, I think Tom did a tremendous job."

That brings us to what's next for the division.

Sonnen believes Gane's championship promotion is imminent. And waiting in the wings appears to be either a rematch with Pereira or a defense against surging contender Josh Hokit . However, the bad blood that's continued to fester between Hokit and Pereira since UFC Freedom 250 — Hokit defeated Derrick Lewis on the same White House card — has opened the door for that fight, said Sonnen, as well as fellow contender Alexander Volkov.

"[UFC is] goin g to elevate Ciryl. They've already got something in place for what they're going to do. The question becomes, who's going to fight Ciryl?" Sonnen said.

"I have a fear that Josh Hokit, who is trying to get the nod against Ciryl over the proverbial battle that he is having with Alex Pereira right now — I fear that Josh, on accident, by way of dismissing Alex, is inadvertently creating a massive fight against Alex. And you're going to have to bring Volkov in at some point, you're going to have to take the risk and do that match."

A fight between Gane and Volkov would be their third, with Gane holding a 2-0 lead in the series. The pair's rematch in December 2024, however, was a highly controversial split decision, which many argued should have gone in favor of the towering Russian. Gane won the first fight via a five-round unanimous decision in June 2021.

In total, Volkov has won six of his past seven bouts since 2022, except for that close Gane rematch.

In his perfect world, Sonnen would give Hokit the next crack at Gane, but he sees Volkov as a factor that could become hard to ignore in the conversation.

"You're going to have to pay an integrity to the rankings at some point," Sonnen said. "They're not going to be able to have Volkov win another fight, whoever that's against, and then not give him the chance. So Volkov is right there. Not to mention he was very competitive with Ciryl. I believe he beat Ciryl and lost the decision, so does Dana White and Hunter Campbell. So, at some point, there is a human element, not to mention he's got the ranking.

"Imagine a card where you're going to do Volkov and Ciryl, and a lot of people for the press conference go, 'Ah.' But on that same card, you put Hokit and Pereira. Now, all of a sudden, much like Arman Tsarukyan and [Mauricio] Ruffy came in to really help and support their own main event [at UFC 331], I think all of a sudden that makes a little bit of sense. Because if you don't do that, then you're going to have to do Volkov versus some form of a title shot one fight from now, and you might not have the coverage of Hokit-Pereira."

images.caption: Tom Aspinall remains sidelined nearly a year after his injuries against Ciryl Gane. (GIUSEPPE CACACE via Getty Images)

articles.title: Ilia Topuria Accuses Justin Gaethje of Cheating at UFC White House Fight, Provides Injury Update
articles.summary: After his loss to Justin Gaethje at UFC's Freedom 250 in June, Ilia Topuria accused the lightweight champion of glove manipulation.
articles.body:
After his loss to Justin Gaethje at UFC's Freedom 250 in June, Ilia Topuria accused the lightweight champion of glove manipulation.

In a post updating his injury status, Topuria said the next time he fights Gaethje, he'll "check Justin's gloves so he doesn't put anything weird on them."

"Final medical tests done. I'm back. To all the clowns who've been talking s--t and counting me out this whole time, here I am," he wrote on social media. "Now let's see who's got the balls. Thanks to everyone for the support. Next time I'll make sure they check Justin's gloves so he doesn't put anything weird on them. See you soon."

Topuria had an undefeated record coming into the fight and was looking to defend his lightweight title for a third time in the fight. Gaethje was competing for the lightweight title for the first time since 2022.

Topuria sustained significant facial damage in the bout, with the fight nearly being stopped before the start of the fourth round. His corner eventually ended the fight before the final round.

As a result of the facial damage, Topuria broke both orbital bones but did not need surgery.

It was by far the most damage Topuria has taken during his career, and it's easy to see why he was quick to accuse Gaethje of cheating. Whether anything will come out of the investigation remains to be seen.

But one thing that is clear is that a rematch between Topuria and Gaethje could be on the way, especially after the bold claim from Topuria on Wednesday.

articles.title: AEW Dynamite Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights From September 16
articles.summary: The September 16 edition of AEW Dynamite aired from the Chartway Arena in Norfolk, Virginia, promising first-time collisions and exciting developments toward All Out.
articles.body:
The September 16 edition of AEW Dynamite aired from the Chartway Arena in Norfolk, Virginia, promising first-time collisions and exciting developments toward All Out.

Will Ospreay, Andrade El Ídolo and Francesco Akira fought The Death Riders' Jon Moxley, Pac and Gabe Kidd. Jamie Hayter fought Lena Kross for the first time one-on-one.

Christian Cage, Adam Copeland, Darby Allin and Steven Borden teamed up to fight FTR, Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight. Nick Wayne hoped to make a statement at the expense of Chris Jericho.

For all the action and drama, check out the results, live grades and highlights below.

Christian Cage, Adam Copeland, Darby Allin and Steven Borden vs. FTR, Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight

Last Time in Action: Darby Allin and Steven Borden won their team debut against Josh Alexander and Mark Davis, and Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight defeated The Young Bucks (Dynamite, September 9). Christian Cage and Adam Copeland defeated The Young Bucks (All In, August 30). FTR lost to Cage and Cope (Double or Nothing, May 24).

Allin and Christian quickly tagged back and forth to decide who would get into it with Fletcher.

Steven got a chance to show off against Dax, including an impressively high Dropkick. The tensions kept building until all eight brawled in the ring into the commercial break.

From the break, the heels isolated The Daredevil and took out Cage and Cope, but Steven was able to make the hot tag and clear the ring until he was alone with Dax.

Dax managed to lay out Steven and set him up for a series of dives by all the heels, but Allin broke up the pin.

Christian caught Dax with a steel chair behind the referee's back then Cope hit him with a Spear. After a final scrap, Allin and Steven hit their Scorpion Death Drop/Coffin Drop combo for the win.

There were eight men in this match, yet this was the Steven show in terms of pace and focus.

He got all the hot tag spots and the pinfall victory at the end. It is clear that Tony Khan is heavily invested in Sting's son and wants to make him the next big thing.

He may just succeed, especially given how good he looks with Allin. The crowd is invested in the new star and is ready to believe.

Knight and Fletcher have been the main focus of recent weeks, including winning the main event last week. It was a bit surprising how little they factored into this match.

It looks likely that The Protostar and The Jet will face Allin and Steven at All Out, which will be the biggest possible challenge for the new star that needs to show he can hang with two of AEW's biggest top star projects.

Steven, Allin, Cope and Christian def. Dax, Cash, Knight and Fletcher by pinfall.

The show started with both team conversing backstage. Christian struggled to play nice while Don Callis questioned if his boys should be No. 1 contenders.

Cope was wearing his new shirt just added on ShopAEW.com.

Stokely Hathaway joined commentary while Callis played manager. Stokely was especially focused on Steven.

In a match filled with present and future top guys in AEW, Steven was easily the most over star in the match.

Steven is still learning, but his Dropkick is amongst the best in AEW. He knows it too because it used it liberally.

articles.title: Tito Ortiz wants to end decades of bad blood with Dana White: 'I've tried to apologize'
articles.summary: "If that bridge could ever be hashed back together between me and Dana, I would love it," said the UFC legend. "But I know Dana. He's not that type of guy."
articles.body:
Tito Ortiz was never afraid to make enemies throughout his legendary MMA career. But in hindsight, the UFC Hall of Famer wishes he could take back one of his greatest rivalries.

As one of the first true superstars amid UFC's early rise, Ortiz lived up to his "Huntington Beach Bad Boy" nickname for reasons that extended beyond the Octagon. His attitude didn't always align with those around him, most notably including UFC CEO Dana White.

White and Ortiz publicly butted heads throughout the latter's entire run with the company from 1997 to 2012. On Wednesday's edition of "The Ariel Helwani Show," the former UFC light heavyweight champion admitted he regrets how he handled his experience with White, and noted he's even tried to reconcile in recent years.

"I've tried to reach out a few times. I've tried to do interviews and apologize, just saying that I'm sorry for what I did. I was a young kid," Ortiz told Uncrowned.

"I said some things about him a few times that I probably shouldn't have. I shouldn't have went over and above, but I didn't understand. Negotiation tactics that I learned, I learned from him — I tried to use his own negotiation tactics on himself, which I shouldn't have done that. I was influenced by others that I shouldn't have been influenced by. I should have thought what I thought and what was right. I made some bad decisions, and I've tried to apologize for that."

One moment in particular stood out for Ortiz when he thought about his greatest regrets in dealing with White. At UFC 84 in May 2008, Ortiz fought Lyoto Machida and infamously showed up at the weigh-ins wearing a T-shirt that read, "Dana is my b****."

"Wearing the T-shirt I did before the Machida fight, I probably shouldn't have did that," Ortiz said. "A few interviews that I said some things, I probably shouldn't have done. But at the time, like I said, I was just trying to fight for my future as a fighter. I know I'm not going to be able to compete for the rest of my life. I knew this company was going to be as big as it is now. So, I was just trying to get paid a little bit more money.

"That was one of the big things that Dana always said: 'Don't talk about money to the public.' But to me, I wanted to take care of my family forever."

Having been one of the UFC's biggest stars of the promotion's early years, Ortiz, 51, is now comfortably phased out of fight life, having not competed in MMA since 2019. Ortiz now runs his own restaurant in Florida, Tito's Cantina , and makes a living there.

He wonders if things would've been different if his relationship with White was better.

"I'm a blue-collar guy now. I still gotta get up, and I gotta work," Ortiz said. "I have a little bit of an advantage by being Tito Ortiz, and I have some amazing fans that respect me and still come to my restaurant. I still do public appearances. I still do public speaking. I do these other things because I made my name as Tito Ortiz, because the UFC has given me that opportunity.

"At the end of the day, I shouldn't have to do these things. I shouldn't have to worry about my bills being paid, because I've fought my a** for 16 years for the UFC and helped them get on the track of where they are right now.

"I'm thankful for the track they gave me and the opportunities they gave me through my career, but it's a double-edged sword. I messed up," Ortiz continued. "It is part of the deal. If that bridge could ever be hashed back together between me and Dana, I would love it. But I know Dana. He's not that type of guy. I know what type of guy he is, and he's not that type of guy.

"It's hurtful, but it's OK. I'm thankful for my fans. My fans have never forgotten about who I am, and I'm thankful for it."

Ortiz's induction into the UFC Hall of Fame in 2012 is arguably the closest thing to reconciliation he's had with White and the promotion since his departure more than a decade ago. Yet, Ortiz still isn't in good enough graces to be treated like anything more than a fan.

When the UFC was in Miami for UFC 327 in April, Ortiz said he was denied a single ticket upon his inquiry. He admitted that the lack of appreciation the promotion has shown for his era of UFC legends bothers him.

"I asked just for one ticket, and they said no. So I ended up buying a ticket. It cost me $1,000. Dana just doesn't like me," Ortiz said.

"I'm not going to sit here and beg. I'm not begging for anything. That's the way he feels, OK. It is what it is. He's gambling millions and millions every night, but take care of the guys that got you here.

"Once again, I don't want anything from him. I laid my own bed. I made it. I'm OK with it. It is what it is. But like former football players, basketball players, they're sitting front row. I think they deserve it. MMA fighters, same thing. Randy Couture, myself, [Quinton] 'Rampage' [Jackson], so many other fighters that have spoken up and have pretty much been erased from UFC. That's one thing they can't do, though, because of the fans — the fans will never forget us."

images.caption: Tito Ortiz (R) and Dana White (L) have had a long and fraught relationship. (Al Powers via Getty Images)

articles.title: Arman Tsarukyan, NHL player? UFC 331 star describes what could've been
articles.summary: Before it was the UFC, Arman Tsarukyan set sights on the NHL.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES – Before he was a UFC superstar and world-famous streamer, Arman Tsarukyan had dreams of being known for his abilities on ice.

Tsarukyan (23-3 MMA, 10-2 UFC) co-headlines Saturday's UFC 331 at Crypto.com Arena ( Paramount+ ) and what a journey it's been. His athletic origins haven't always been fight-centric, Tsarukyan revealed Wednesday. Apparently, hockey was his first love and is still something he's passionate about.

"I wanted to be a hockey player," Tsarukyan told MMA Junkie and other reporters at a pre-fight news conference Wednesday. "My dream was to go to the U.S. and play in the NHL. But I couldn't be a good hockey player, and then I started working. I didn't like working, and I became a fighter. Because of fighting, now I'm in U.S. and fighting in the best promotion in UFC. My hockey career was so good. I love hockey and when I have time even now sometimes I play."

Born in Armenia, Tsarukyan doesn't associate with a specific NHL team. However, his favorite player he revealed without hesitation.

"I like (Alexander) Ovechkin ," Tsarukyan said.

How far Tsarukyan would've gone in hockey remains unclear, but it's almost certainly not as far as he's gone in the fight world. A win Saturday over Mauricio Ruffy could get him the long-awaited title shot he's dreamed of.

"Yeah, 100 percent," Tsarukyan said of what his odds are of fighting for gold should he win Saturday.

Despite radiating confidence, Tsarukyan didn't hold back on his compliments of Ruffy (14-2 MMA, 5-1 UFC), the tricky and flashy striker who trains alongside former UFC middleweight champion Israel Adesanya and current UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski . While Tsarukayn admitted Ruffy is a unique test unlike any he's faced before, his prediction didn't waver. The biggest thing he thinks he needs to do is weather the storm, and the fight will be his.

"You cannot compare Adesanya with me," Tsarukyan said. "You cannot compare Volkanovski with me. It's completely different fighters. He has the power and he has good striking, but I'm better everywhere with my wrestling and my striking that I can mix. I can over-strike him."

"... He has a really awkward style. I've never faced anybody like his striking. It's going to be a little bit dangerous in the first round, but second round should be good."

articles.title: Jon Jones Return Teased by Gable Steveson, Next Fight Predicted in New Video
articles.summary: Jon Jones hasn't fought since November 2024, when he successfully defended his heavyweight title, and Gable Steveson believes he could come back to claim the title once again.
articles.body:
Jon Jones hasn't fought since November 2024, when he successfully defended his heavyweight title, and Gable Steveson believes he could come back to claim the title once again.

Steveson teased a possible title fight for Jones if he chooses to return to the UFC.

"I called Jon today, and he's honored to have the opportunity to maybe come back," Steveson said. "He's always had gold around his waist."

Jones beat Stipe Miocic at UFC 309 to defend his heavyweight title for the first time, and he shortly after expressed interest in a heavyweight title unification bout with Tom Aspinall.

Jones has since retired, but there have been several indications that he's not done fighting.

He reentered the UFC's drug-testing pool last July, shortly after the UFC 250 event at the White House was announced, though he ended up not being on the card for that event.

Now could be the perfect time for him to officially make his return.

Aspinall vacated the UFC heavyweight title due to "ongoing complications" with his eye, meaning Ciryl Gane was promoted to the undisputed champion. Jones may have wanted to fight Aspinall initially, but he might instead have the chance to take back the title against Gane.

articles.title: Amy Broadhurst continues comeback at European championships: 'This will be my last shot at the Olympics'
articles.summary: Amy Broadhurst is continuing her boxing comeback after becoming a mother; A World and European gold medallist for Ireland, Broadhurst has switched to GB and will box for Britain at the European Championships, her first major tournament since having a baby
articles.body:
Amy Broadhurst, a former World and European gold medallist for Ireland, will be part of the squad boxing for Britain.

Broadhurst, a key sparring partner for Katie Taylor for the Irish legend's first iconic victory over Amanda Serrano, switched from Ireland to Britain ahead of Paris 2024 as she sought to qualify for the Olympic Games.

These European championships will be her first major championships since returning to competition after the birth of her baby boy.

"It's tough but we're making it work and I'm very lucky to have the support around me," Broadhurst told Sky Sports . "He's at the right age now where this is possible.

"He'll come to Bulgaria with me and he comes to Sheffield every second week with me," she continued. "Those weeks are tough because you're doing two jobs then.

"This is my last shot at the Olympics. So they know after this it's all said and done."

These Europeans will be a key step on a journey that she hopes will eventually take her to LA 2028. But her return to boxing has already been eventful. The first bout in her comeback earlier this year saw her drawn against her old team.

"My first fight back after two years was against Ireland. So that was a mad situation," she said.

"I was trying to control my feelings because obviously a lot of [stuff] went on with that whole situation.

"I knew going in that I was going to do okay. But there was just a lot of ill feelings on both behalfs. I think I handled it very well. I shook hands with the coach and I showed respect. That was probably the main thing, not to get sucked into the emotional part of it. It was get in, box and move on. It was like closing the chapter on something. We shook hands and then that's it."

She didn't box Ireland's top lightweight then but that could potentially happen in Sofia. Kellie Harrington, Ireland's two-time Olympic champion, has entered these Europeans.

"I was her sparring partner for the 2021 Games," Broadhurst said. "I was brought over to Tokyo.

"We've shared the ring many times and it would be a spicy fight.

"You could meet each other," Broadhurst noted. "You just don't know what's going to happen.

images.caption: Image: Broadhurst will box for GB at the European championships in Bulgaria.
Image: Amy Broadhurst is a World Championships gold medallist taking one last chance to reach the Olympic Games.

articles.title: MMA: Irish fighter Adam Darby reflects on journey to UFC after earning Dana White Contender Series contract
articles.summary: Dublin mixed martial artist Adam Darby says more than a decade of hard work came "to fruition" after becoming the first Irish fighter to earn a UFC contract through Dana White's Contender Series.
articles.body:
Mixed martial artist Adam Darby says more than a decade of hard work came "to fruition" after becoming the first Irish fighter to earn a UFC contract through Dana White's Contender Series.

Darby (8-1) secured his place on the UFC roster with an impressive TKO victory over American Patrick Rivera (13-5) in Las Vegas on 1 September.

The welterweight dominated Rivera before the bout ended in the third round via doctor stoppage.

Darby was one of five fighters awarded UFC contracts on the night, completing an arduous journey which included a 20-second defeat by Mush Aslani and a 17-month absence because of a serious hand injury.

"I was just sitting there thinking to myself, well, that's 10-plus years of work all coming to fruition," Darby told BBC Sport NI.

The Dubliner had controlled the contest against Rivera but was hoping the fight would continue long enough for him to secure a more emphatic finish.

"I was saying to the referee, 'Don't stop it, he's good, he's good,'" he said.

"I knew he was done, but I wanted a highlight-reel finish. The ref recognised the damage he was taking and pulled the plug on it.

"I went in there to put on a show, and I think I delivered."

Liverpool's Liam McCracken also competed on the card but missed out on a UFC contract after suffering a knockout defeat by Silvestre Sanchez in a thrilling lightweight contest.

The former Cage Warriors fighter's journey started when his father enrolled him in kickboxing, but upon discovering MMA, he was hooked.

"Once I had my first day in MMA, that was it," he said.

"That was me for the rest of my life, and now here we are over 10 years later and I'm a professional UFC fighter."

That conviction was evident in a note Darby wrote in 2018 and shared on social media following his Contender Series victory.

It read: "One life, one chance, UFC or nothing."

"Visualisation is very important, but you can't sit in your bedroom looking in the mirror saying, 'I'm the best of the best,' and not training and backing it up," he said.

"You have to set some goals and put the work in to get to where you want to be. I had to put the work in."

But the Clongriffin fighter, who is currently on a seven-fight winning streak, encountered several setbacks in pursuit of his UFC dream.

He entered his second professional fight believing he was 'the best guy in the world', only to suffer a standing TKO defeat by Aslani.

"For a lot of people that might finish their career," he said.

"But for me, that loss made me reflect, 'where am I going to go from here?'

"You can't let something like that set you back. Life's going to hit you hard, but you have to be able to come back from it."

A greater obstacle followed when Darby suffered serious hand and finger injuries before Cage Warriors 170 bout in March 2024, requiring multiple operations and 17 months away from competition.

"I snapped my finger in half, I broke my hand, I had to have multiple surgeries to get it back right," Darby said.

"I was told, 'You probably won't fight again, you won't be able to punch with that.'

"That was two and a half years ago, and here I am now."

Darby hopes his achievement can inspire another generation of Irish fighters to follow him into the UFC.

"It's inspiring to think somebody watching me in five or 10 years' time in the UFC might say, 'I saw Adam Darby do it so I knew I could do it,'" he said.

"The area I come from, not a lot of people make it out like this and do so well.

"So it's good to show people that you can earn an honest living and do fighting and make some money out of it."

The Team Ryano fighter believes the standard of Irish MMA has risen significantly, with more fighters now able to dedicate themselves fully to the sport.

"The standard of MMA in Ireland has improved so much. The fighters before us worked multiple jobs their whole career, now everybody is training full-time," he said.

"Looking at the guys coming through at Cage Warriors, Paddy McCorry, Ger Harris, Solomon Simon, these guys are only 12 to 24 months away from the UFC."

Having spent more than a decade trying to reach the promotion, Darby is now targeting his UFC debut before the end of the year.

"I'll definitely be targeting one more fight this year, but it's up to UFC now," he said.

"I've always told them I'm ready to fight whenever they want me to."

images.caption: Image caption, Adam Darby earned a UFC deal after beating Patrick Rivera in Las Vegas
Image caption, Darby has eight wins and one defeat from nine professional bouts
Image caption, Darby suffered a broken hand in March 2024 before returning to the cage after a 17-month absence in April 2025

articles.title: Marie McManamon to fight Yu Yau Pui on the undercard Paul Elliott's heavyweight world title fight against Shamil Erdogan
articles.summary: Britain's Marie McManamon will meet Hong Kong Muay Thai star Yu Yau Pui on the undercard of Paul Elliott's heavyweight title fight; Watch ONE Fight Night 48 live on Sky Sports in the early hours of Saturday October 3
articles.body:
McManamon is one of the UK's premier female Muay Thai athletes. A force in the ring, she has used her relentless cardio and whipping kicks to earn both Victory League and Roar Fighting Championship Titles.

Coming off a loss to Selina Flores, McManamon, a former ONE world title challenger, is going straight back into another top-level contest.

A dangerous striker who can end a contest at any given moment, Yu Yau Pui began competing in the weekly ONE Friday Fights series in 2023 and after four knockout wins in five fights, the Chinese striker won a lucrative $100,000 contract to ONE Championship.

ONE Fight Night 48, live on Sky Sports in the early hours of Saturday October 3, will be headlined by Middlesbrough's Paul Elliott in a ONE Championship heavyweight world title bout against Shamil Erdogan.

The card also features America's Luke Lessei versus England's Charlie Guest in an important Muay Thai match which will see the winner push for a crack at Nico Carrillo's featherweight title.

Watch ONE Fight Night 48 live on Sky Sports in the early hours of Saturday October 3.
